# ASUR Open Questions (SPEC-GAPs)

Every place the spec/docs/PDF were silent or divergent. Each has a **conservative,
fail-closed default** that honors the 8 invariants, so building can proceed safely
until a human decides otherwise. **Never guess beyond the default — if a gap blocks,
STOP.**

Status values: `open` (default in force, awaiting human) · `resolved` (human or ADR
decided) · `deferred` (not needed until a later phase).

 | G30 | Can we **empirically prove the viral-check score predicts real-world performance** (the user's #1 "worth real money" ask: score 200–500 real Reels/Shorts before seeing their views, then show the score predicts performance)? The checker scores **input quality vs documented signals** and by ASUR-HONEST-01 **cannot emit a predicted-views/%viral number**, so "predicts performance" can only mean a **correlation measured after the fact**, not a predictor. Fetching real clips + view counts needs the network + the user's own credentials, which §4 (no test touches the network) and §11 (paid/cloud/API is human-gated) forbid inside the stdlib core / pytest suite | **Blind correlation study, three separated pieces, never a predictor.** (1) A **human-gated collector** tool that lives **outside** `asur/` stdlib core and **outside** pytest (never imported by core, never run in CI); the human runs it with their own credentials to pull N clips + metadata and writes a dataset dir with the **view counts sealed** in a separate file. (2) A **blind-scoring** harness (stdlib-only): machine auto-derives only **observable** `platform_facts` (aspect ratio, resolution, captions-present, audio-present, watermark) via ffprobe + the existing faster-whisper adapter; the **judgment-call** booleans (`delivers_promise`, `strong_first_three_seconds`) come from a **blind human rater** who watches each clip **without** seeing its view count (never invented, §7); then `build_viral_view → score_all + decide_verdict` per clip with the views **still sealed**. (3) An **offline correlation report** (stdlib-only, no network): unseal the views, compute **Spearman rank correlation** per dimension + verdict-vs-performance, with honest confidence caveats. **Never** emit a %viral/predicted-views number (ASUR-HONEST-01 + the existing `test_no_single_viral_percentage_anywhere` guard). The honest correlation result is itself the sellable asset. Tests cover the stdlib scoring+correlation math on tiny fixtures only; the collector + any real clip/model work is `@pytest.mark.integration` or entirely outside pytest | open (V1a spine + V1b human-gated collector landed; V1c real 200–500-clip study is human-driven and remains) | V1a — `asur/viral_check/validation/{derive,score_blind,correlate}.py` + `tests/test_viral_validation_v1a.py` + `tests/fixtures/viral_validation/demo-study/` (blind Spearman correlation, scorer never opens sealed views, no %viral number). V1b — `studio/validation/collect.py` (human-gated collector: human-prepared JSON list → sealed dataset in the V1a schema; never logs in / calls an API / downloads / scores; outside `asur/` + not in pytest; refuses overwrite, rejects clips with no observed public view count) |

The Life Mentor (`LM-G*`) and Weekly Tracker (`WT-G*`) questions moved with
those products to https://github.com/prathamshukla28/life-os.

## How to resolve
Pick a row, decide, and either (a) accept the default (mark `resolved`, note
"default accepted"), or (b) choose an alternative — which requires a new ADR in
`docs/adr/` and a SPEC update. Record the resolver in the last column.
